sections.markdown:
## C2 — Zipper merge continuation facts, then confusable pairs and knowledge-graph hints: meeting versus following a school bus, hill wheel directions, acceleration versus deceleration lanes and passing lanes
Continuation facts for the zipper merge and remaining parking and exit steps, plus confusable pairs among school bus directions, hill parking, highway lanes and passing; each block ties to one handbook page, and hint metadata sits only in the trailing line of a block.

FACT_ID: sec10-R01 | anchor: A08
The zipper merge, also called the late merge, means using both lanes right up to the merge area and then taking turns easing into the lane that stays open. [A08]
Why it matters: group zipper merge; difficulty medium.
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0091]

FACT_ID: sec10-R02 | anchor: A08
The manual presents the zipper merge as a new strategy for drivers who were taught to merge early, because merging early can bring unexpected and dangerous lane switching, collisions and road rage. [A08]
Why it matters: group zipper merge; confusable early merge versus late merge.
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0091]

FACT_ID: sec10-R03 | anchor: A08
Once a lane closed ahead sign appears and traffic starts to back up, keep to your current lane until the merge point, then take turns with other drivers to move over safely and smoothly. [A08]
Why it matters: group zipper merge; difficulty medium.
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0091]

FACT_ID: sec10-R04 | anchor: A08
No law requires the zipper merge, but it is a best practice, especially where a lane is closed in a construction zone. [A08]
Why it matters: group zipper merge; confusable best practice versus legal requirement.
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0091]

FACT_ID: sec10-R05 | anchor: A08
The zipper merge narrows the speed difference between lanes, which makes changing lanes easier and safer, and it can shorten the overall traffic backup by as much as 40%. [A08]
Why it matters: group zipper merge; difficulty medium.
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0091]

FACT_ID: sec10-R06 | anchor: A08
Other benefits listed are less congestion on the interstate, a sense of fairness because all lanes move at the same rate, and fewer road rage incidents. [A08]
Why it matters: group zipper merge; difficulty low.
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0091]

FACT_ID: sec10-R07 | anchor: A09
When traffic is moving at highway speed with no backups, it makes sense to move over early to the lane that will stay open, and the bottom line is to merge when it is safe. [A09]
Why it matters: group zipper merge; confusable heavy slow traffic versus free-flowing traffic.
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0092]

FACT_ID: sec10-R08 | anchor: A01
Always park in a designated parking area. [A01]
Why it matters: group parking; difficulty low.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0084]

FACT_ID: sec10-R09 | anchor: A01
Following a stopped school bus always requires a stop on any highway, while meeting one from the opposite direction is excused only on a multi-lane highway or private road. [A01]
Why it matters: group school buses; confusable following versus meeting.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0084]

FACT_ID: sec10-R10 | anchor: A03
Parallel parking also ends with the vehicle no more than 18 inches from the curb or edge of pavement. [A03]
Why it matters: group parking; difficulty low.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0086]

FACT_ID: sec10-R11 | anchor: A02
Finish entering a perpendicular or angle space by moving to the front of it, stopping and securing the vehicle. [A02]
Why it matters: group parking; difficulty low.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0085]

FACT_ID: sec10-R12 | anchor: A04
When pulling out of a parallel space, make sure your front bumper will clear the vehicle ahead, and if it will not, reverse and correct your steering. [A04]
Why it matters: group parking; difficulty medium.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0087]

FACT_ID: sec10-R13 | anchor: A04
When leaving any parking space, signal, use your mirrors, look over your shoulder for traffic and yield the right-of-way. [A04]
Why it matters: group parking; difficulty low.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0087]

FACT_ID: sec10-R14 | anchor: A04
Downhill parking and uphill parking without a curb both turn the wheels to the right, while uphill parking beside a curb turns them toward the center of the street. [A04]
Why it matters: group hill parking; confusable uphill with curb versus without curb.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0087]

FACT_ID: sec10-R15 | anchor: A06
The deceleration lane, used to slow for an exit, lies to the right of the roadway before you reach the ramp, whereas you keep your speed until you move into it. [A06]
Why it matters: group highways; confusable acceleration lane versus deceleration lane.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0089]

FACT_ID: sec10-R16 | anchor: A06
The left-most lane of a multi-lane road is the passing lane, while the shoulder on the right is for emergency stops only and is never used to pass. [A06]
Why it matters: group passing; confusable left lane versus shoulder.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0089]

FACT_ID: sec10-R17 | anchor: A07
The driver passing must keep going until the whole front of the passed vehicle shows in the rearview mirror, while the driver being passed stays in lane at a steady speed. [A07]
Why it matters: group passing; confusable passing driver versus driver being passed.
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0090]
